answer: A willow grove on the riverbank gives each agent one coppiced stool to tend all year. When the sun sets through the notch on the western horizon, the ten-day cutting season opens, and each agent cuts rods from their own stool and weaves a wicker creel. The warden weighs the creel and counts its rods against last year's entry in the grove book, and a creel with borrowed rods or a copied weave fails the count and loses the stool for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand stools tended all year and a thousand creels woven by hand inside ten days.
